trust_decision.summary: Attacker-controlled SHC/JWT input is decompressed before it is validated: when the JOSE header says zip=DEF, the base64-decoded segment is handed to java.util.zip.Inflater and drained in a while(!inflater.finished()) loop that never handles a 0-byte return, so an empty, truncated or dictionary-needing stream spins forever; the trust boundary is that payload segment at the Inflater call, and the published fix adds the termination guard only in the r5 class.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'SHCParser DEFLATE infinite loop'; the only method with that name in the class the summary names is the public static inflate(byte[]), whose loop at 462-466 writes a 0-byte result and spins with no exit.

fix_sites.entry_point: SHCParser.inflate(byte[]) public static API, reached from Manager.parse(..., FhirFormat.SHC) -> SHCParser.parse(InputStream) -> decodeJWT -> inflate when the JWT header has zip=DEF, and from SHLParser.processContent for content-type application/smart-health-card
SHCParser.decodeJWT(...) -> checkSignature -> verifySignature, i.e. the JWS signature-verification path (reached only once a JWKS document has been fetched for the iss URL)
fix_sites.module_kind: library parser (element model), private helper on the signature path, org.hl7.fhir.r5

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The r4b class is the legacy R4B copy of the same parser: the validator CLI, SHL flow and ResourceChecker only build org.hl7.fhir.r5.elementmodel.SHCParser, and nothing in this repo detects or routes SHC content into the r4b Manager, so a solver can call it a compatibility API that no shipping path reaches.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A DEFLATE payload that produces no output must degrade gracefully rather than throw: the fix's own regression asserts inflate(new byte[0]) returns normally, and decodeJWT feeds whatever comes back to the JSON parser so a truncated stream surfaces as a structured 'Unable to decode JWT token' error; the MAX_ALLOWED_SHC_LENGTH check at 282-284 is QR-only and advisory (logError, no reject) while the JSON verifiableCredential file form legitimately carries longer tokens, so an over-broad fix that turns the loop into a hard reject or a size limit breaks valid file-download cards.

O6_input_shapes: empty byte[] (zero-length DEFLATE payload - Inflater returns 0 forever at the pinned commit)
truncated / incomplete DEFLATE stream (needsInput() true while finished() stays false)
stream requiring a preset dictionary (needsDictionary() true)
valid complete DEFLATE stream (count>0 path must be byte-identical after the fix)
both carriers of the same shape: the zip=DEF JWT payload segment and the JWS payload on the signature path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: r4b SHC parsing: Manager.parse(..., FhirFormat.SHC) -> r4b SHCParser.parse(InputStream) -> decodeJWT -> inflate when the JWT header carries zip=DEF; identical unguarded zero-count loop, untouched by both published commits
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: legacy R4B duplicate of an r5-only advisory; no in-repo content detection or CLI path builds the r4b parser, so it is 'not the parser under test'
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different Maven module (org.hl7.fhir.r4b) with the same package name as the r5 class; 1 file away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: r4b public static SHCParser.inflate(byte[]) invoked directly by a library consumer - the same unprotected loop exposed as a low-level utility API
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a static helper on a legacy parser class; callers of the documented r5 API never touch it, so it reads as dead compatibility code
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the r4b parse route, 1 module from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a DEFLATE branch for the JWE payload before it is handed to new SHCParser(context).parse(...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SHL already unwraps a JWE and forwards application/smart-health-card content into SHCParser; a maintainer adding JWE zip=DEF support would paste the same Inflater drain loop here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a decompress()-style helper on the r4b JWT path (r4b has no signature verification, so only the one inflate copy exists today)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the r4b class is maintained by copying r5 changes across; adding signature verification later would duplicate the r5 decompress loop verbatim.

O9_family: unbounded decompression loop / resource exhaustion (CWE-835, CWE-400, CWE-20)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build from the root pom.xml (maven.compiler.release 17, JUnit Jupiter 5.14, surefire 3.5.3)
O10_build.project_tests: No SHC parser test exists at the pinned commit; the first fix commit adds org.hl7.fhir.r5/src/test/java/org/hl7/fhir/r5/elementmodel/SHCParserTests.java (one JUnit 5 test calling SHCParser.inflate(new byte[0])). Tests elsewhere in org.hl7.fhir.validation need downloaded FHIR packages/network.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add a 0-byte break to the inflate(byte[]) loop the report names, re-run the reproduction through decodeJWT, and stop - leaving the decompress loop 45 lines below in the same file and the r4b copy open.
